question: What is Edward Jones's advisor attrition rate compared to Merrill's?

claims.text: Edward Jones's 3Q25 10-Q (published 2025-11-07) reports financial advisor attrition of 6.1% for the third quarter of 2025, against 4.7% in the prior-year quarter. For the nine-month period it reports 6.0%, against 5.1%.

The same 3Q25 10-Q (published 2025-11-07) says attrition was 6.1% 'as a result of a variety of factors, including a rise in financial advisor departures with tenure of five years or less.' It ended the quarter with 20,429 financial advisors.

Edward Jones's 2Q25 10-Q (published 2025-08-08) defines Attrition % as 'the annualized number of financial advisors that left or retired from the Partnership during the period compared to the total number of financial advisors as of period end.'

Edward Jones's 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) names attrition as a risk. It says the Partnership 'may experience increased financial advisor attrition due to increased competition' and that lower firm profitability could 'increase the Partnership's attrition rates.'

adjacent.text: On the 2Q26 Bank of America earnings call (published 2026-07-14, GWIM segment), CFO Alastair Borthwick said 'adviser attrition is now at near historic lows.' He gave no percentage.
adjacent.differs_because: This is a qualitative remark from the CFO on a GWIM-segment call, with no attrition rate. It cannot be compared with Edward Jones's 6.1% or 6.0% figures.

adjacent.text: Edward Jones's 2Q25 10-Q (published 2025-08-08) shows financial advisors at period end of 20,309, against 19,589 a year earlier (+4%).
adjacent.differs_because: Net advisor headcount change is not attrition: it nets hires against departures.

adjacent.text: Bank of America's November 2025 investor day deck (GWIM segment) shows more than 15K wealth advisors for Merrill | Private Bank. This is a headcount, not an attrition rate.
adjacent.differs_because: Net advisor headcount change is not attrition: it nets hires against departures. The figure also covers the GWIM segment (Merrill plus the Private Bank), not Merrill alone.

gaps.what: Neither firm discloses advisor attrition on a comparable basis. Edward Jones publishes a quarterly attrition percentage. In the evidence provided, Merrill has no numeric attrition rate, only management's qualitative 'near historic lows' comment.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America earnings supplements or investor-day disclosures for a Merrill advisor attrition or retention rate, if one is published. Otherwise, recruiter or industry-tracker data, which would be indicative only.

gaps.what: Merrill does not report standalone results.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America GWIM segment disclosures (10-K, 10-Q, earnings supplement).
